Title: GAIL – IEW 2025
description: At India Energy Week 2025, hosted at the state-of-the-art Yashobhoomi Convention Centre in New Delhi, GAIL (India) Limited envisioned more than just a presence — they wanted a powerful expression of their identity. Their ask was simple yet ambitious: create an experience that reflects not only their technical strength and nationwide infrastructure but also their commitment to innovation, sustainability, and public engagement. That’s where Omesa stepped in — not as stall fabricators, but as storytellers in space.
shortDesc: At India Energy Week 2025, hosted at the state-of-the-art Yashobhoomi Convention Centre in New Delhi
desc1: From the beginning, it was clear this couldn’t be approached as a conventional layout with printed panels and demo counters. GAIL wanted a pavilion that could spark curiosity, deliver knowledge, and connect emotionally — a place where a PSU could feel anything but bureaucratic. Our design narrative began by zooming out: instead of just showcasing what GAIL does, we explored why it matters — to the country, the environment, and the everyday citizen. This deeper narrative formed the basis of our design.
desc2: At the heart of the pavilion stood a glowing, suspended central cube, wrapped in GAIL’s identity — bold, kinetic, and unmistakable from across the exhibition floor. This was more than a visual anchor; it was a symbol of energy and momentum. Once inside, visitors moved through multi-sensory zones. One of the most arresting elements was a digital, interactive map of India, tracing GAIL’s vast national gas grid. Visitors could engage directly with the screen — zooming in on pipelines, discovering project locations, and seeing how the network touches their own cities and states.
desc3: Nearby, touchscreen kiosks hosted dynamic quizzes and informative modules — simplifying complex data into digestible, engaging formats. These weren’t passive displays; they were designed for interaction. For many, the real thrill came from stepping into the CNG driving simulator, a motion-integrated setup that replicated the clean energy transport experience with remarkable realism. Kids, professionals, and officials alike queued up for a glimpse of how energy flows through movement — and how GAIL powers it.
desc4:
But what truly stopped people in their tracks was the robotic ballet installation. A robotic arm mirrored the poised movements of a live ballerina on screen, set against a pulsing kinetic LED backdrop. The harmony of machinery and motion, of grace and precision, felt almost surreal — and entirely intentional. It was the brand’s philosophy translated into art: structured, graceful, futuristic.
Behind the scenes, this level of experience required relentless precision and rapid execution. With a fabrication window of just 15 days, we worked across shifts to build and pre-fit every element — from modular frameworks and LED integrations to curated lighting and live greenery. The stall was constructed using a mix of powder-coated metal, layered acrylics, CNC-cut structures, and sustainable surface treatments, in keeping with the event’s environmental ethos.
desc5: Over three days, the GAIL pavilion saw more than 12,000 visitors, including top-tier government officials, global energy delegates, and thousands of students and engineers. The stall didn’t just attract attention — it started conversations. People lingered, explored, interacted, and posted. The buzz wasn’t forced; it was built into the experience.
desc6: For GAIL, the pavilion became a living embodiment of their brand. For us, it was a masterclass in how spatial design — when infused with emotion, clarity, and technology — can transform a corporate narrative into a public experience. It’s projects like these that remind us: when design, storytelling, and execution come together, a stall doesn’t just showcase a brand — it becomes one.

Title: LT FOODS – WORLD FOOD 2023
description: At World Food India 2023, held in New Delhi, LT Foods — a 70-year-old legacy brand — set out to showcase not just products, but a new direction. Known for Daawat and a trusted presence in rice and staple foods, LT Foods was evolving into something bigger: a global FMCG brand with a conscience. And they chose this event to make that shift visible, tangible, and memorable. Omesa was brought in to translate this vision into a space that could do more than just inform — it had to evoke, engage, and reposition.
shortDesc: At World Food India 2023, held in New Delhi, LT Foods — a 70-year-old legacy brand
desc1: The transformation began with intent. This wasn’t about filling up square footage with products. It was about storytelling — about taking the visitor on a journey from the farms of Punjab to global supermarket shelves. The overarching theme, “Nurturing Goodness,” anchored every design decision. It represented the care LT Foods puts into its sourcing, the relationships it builds with farmers, and the thought it gives to sustainability, innovation, and consumer health.
desc2: The pavilion design was open, inviting, and deeply interactive. Upon entering, visitors were greeted with vibrant digital storytelling panels that traced LT Foods’ growth, impact, and future ambitions — all framed in warm, natural materials and soft lighting that conveyed both heritage and optimism. Every touchpoint was built around discovery. An interactive global map console allowed users to explore the company's international presence and product journeys across continents. Large-scale LED screens told stories of farmer partnerships, sustainable rice cultivation, and technology-driven quality control — breaking down complex systems into visual, human-centered narratives.
desc3: One of the most powerful elements was the “Growing Rice Sustainably” wall, a hands-on display that highlighted how LT Foods supports thousands of farmers through agri-extension programs, fair trade practices, and resource-efficient cultivation methods. It brought agriculture to the forefront in a way that felt accessible, not corporate. Children, policy-makers, and global buyers alike interacted with the display, leaving with a clearer understanding of the values behind the products.
desc4: The storytelling didn’t end at information — it extended into taste and experience. A standout section of the pavilion was the Kameda Food Street, a vibrant corner that celebrated LT Foods’ bold foray into rice-based snacking. Here, visitors could sample Kari Kari, a premium snack brand offering unexpected global flavor pairings. From Salt & Pepperto Soy Sesame, and from Thai Wai to Kolkata-style Jhalmoorie, the flavors were crafted live by professional chefs — creating a bustling, aroma-filled zone where product met culture. Every dish had a story, and every bite reinforced LT Foods’ new personality: experimental, urban, and globally relevant.
desc5: Behind the scenes, Omesa managed end-to-end fabrication and spatial storytelling, delivering a finely tuned experience in a limited setup timeline. The materials — from wood textures and ambient lighting to branded orange architectural beams — brought together LT Foods' Indian roots and global aspirations. The design created fluid pathways for movement, while pausing areas allowed stakeholders to sit, engage, and absorb the messaging at their own pace.
desc6:
But beyond the layout and visuals, what made this pavilion stand out was its intention. This was more than a showcase — it was a moment of brand redefinition. From a rice manufacturer to a global food innovation company, LT Foods used the event to show that its purpose had outgrown its product. What visitors saw wasn’t just a booth — it was a signal. A statement of what the brand was becoming.
In the end, LT Foods didn’t just gain visibility at World Food India — they reclaimed their narrative. For Omesa, this project was a masterclass in how to turn strategy into experience, and experience into memory. A space that once might have displayed SKUs now delivered stories — and those stories left a lasting impact.

Title: Greenko – ICGH 24
description: At ICGH 2024, hosted at the cutting-edge Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, AM Green, a Greenko initiative, marked its presence with purpose. Unlike most exhibitors who treated their booth as a platform to display — AM Green approached it as a space to declare intent. Their vision for India’s clean hydrogen future wasn’t to be told in charts and one-pagers — it had to be felt, walked through, and experienced in three dimensions. When Omesa was brought in to design and build the space, the ask wasn’t just about fabrication — it was to create a live brand experience. One that could hold gravity, spark curiosity, invite dialogue, and still make space for stillness.
shortDesc: At ICGH 2024, hosted at the cutting-edge Yashobhoomi Convention Centre, AM Green, a Greenko initiative, marked its presence with purpose.
desc1: The design began with presence. The structure stood tall and grounded — a minimal yet confident frame made from vertical wood-finish fins, accented with warm amber light. It was architectural without being cold, sleek without losing soul. The AM Green logo, subtly backlit, sat atop the pavilion like a quiet affirmation. From afar, the stall was clearly visible — but it didn’t compete for attention. Instead, it had a kind of assuredness that made people walk toward it. It didn’t beckon with gimmicks; it simply stood with clarity, like the future it represented.
desc2: Once inside, the energy shifted. The space opened up into a central exhibit zone, where models and scaled infrastructure layouts demonstrated AM Green’s green hydrogen ecosystems, integrated renewable systems, and scalable solutions. Visitors weren’t bombarded with messaging. Instead, the information was choreographed — through immersive LED content walls that played out AM Green’s work with the World Economic Forum, global renewable partners, and the technology driving their transition. These weren’t pitch decks on screen. They were narratives in motion, framed in design that respected the intelligence and attention of the audience.
desc3: We didn’t just plan for footfall — we planned for flow. The space moved in gradients — from the open product island to the more conversational pockets, all the way to the lounge at the rear, subtly shielded by the structural frame. Here, we created a semi-private discussion area, tucked yet not hidden, using natural greenery and material textures to soften the transition. It was in this zone that the real connections happened — where policy makers pulled up chairs, where business leads discussed collaborations, and where serious questions about India’s decarbonisation roadmap were asked and answered over quiet conversations.
desc4:
Every material decision was made with intention. We used modular aluminum structures for flexibility and sustainability, finished with engineered wood laminates that offered richness without waste. The lighting was human-scale — warm, indirect, and layered — eliminating the harsh glare that usually dominates exhibition halls. We brought in planters with vertical greens not just for aesthetic comfort but to signal the intersection of technology and ecology — the very heart of AM Green’s vision. Even the flooring was chosen to absorb light and reduce distraction, allowing eyes to settle on interaction, not reflection.

And yet, what elevated the space wasn’t the build alone — it was the invisible choreography of brand and behavior. Delegates didn’t just pass through. They paused. They engaged. Some returned more than once. We noticed something telling — people came in groups, but dispersed within the space. Some leaned into the model, others absorbed the screen content, and a few walked directly into the lounge. The space anticipated multiple ways of being present — active, observational, conversational. It allowed for it all, without pushing one agenda. That is the power of intuitive design.
desc5: Throughout the event, AM Green’s booth became a kind of anchor point — not loud, but magnetic. It drew in senior leaders, policy makers, energy experts, and international delegates, not with flashy screens or bold colors, but with architectural calm and narrative depth. There was something about the space that made people linger — a rare phenomenon at high-stimulus exhibitions. Perhaps it was the balance of form and message. Perhaps it was the way the structure echoed the brand’s core value: energy that is intelligent, scalable, and deeply human.
desc6: For Omesa, this wasn’t just a design project — it was a manifestation of what we believe in: that experiential marketing isn’t about building booths; it’s about building meaningful brand moments. It’s about crafting environments that extend the brand’s voice into form, into texture, into space. With AM Green at ICGH 2024, we created more than a pavilion — we created a moment of pause in a fast-moving sector, where the future of green energy wasn’t just discussed — it was quietly, confidently felt.
